transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Clarke (Redwood AE), Nina Patel (Redwood SE), Arjun Mehta (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Argus Head of Search), Priya Rao (Argus ML Eng), Elena Gomez (Argus CTO), Samir Das (Argus Platform)

Auto-generated Summary: Initial discovery; Argus evaluating embeddings + reranking for product search. Agreed to run benchmarks and exchange security docs.

[00:00] Jamie Clarke: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jamie from Redwood, good to meet you all. we've got Nina and Arjun from our solutions team here too. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Marcus Lee: Yeah thanks Jamie, good to be here. quick intros - I'm Marcus, I run search at Argus. with me is Priya, our ML engineer, Elena our CTO and Samir who manages infra.
[00:15] Nina Patel: Great, quick agenda from our side: understand your current stack, what you want from embeddings/reranking, latency and throughput targets, and security constraints.
[00:22] Priya Rao: Sounds good. to frame it - we run a product search, about 40M SKUs, annual queries ~150M, peak QPS around 120 during promos. current system: ES for inverted index + a lightweight reranker on CPU. looking to move to sem search + dense rerank for better relevance.
[00:35] Arjun Mehta: Nice, and are you currently storing vectors in a vector DB or co-locating them in ES?
[00:39] Priya Rao: We've been prototyping with OpenSearch vector plugin but hitting scaling issues. also tried a small Milvus cluster for a PoC, but ops cost and QA were painful.
[00:48] Elena Gomez: Main drivers: relevance improvements, reduce manual rules. Secondary is cost predictability - we want to avoid surprise cloud GPU bills.
[00:57] Jamie Clarke: Got it. high level, Redwood can host embeddings and reranking on our hosted API, or you can go dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) or private deployment in your VPC. tradeoffs are predictability and isolation vs easiest path.
[01:10] Marcus Lee: Can you explain how integration with our vector DB would look? we ideally want to keep our inverted index in ES for recall and do a hybrid search - bm25 shortlist then embedding-based rerank.
[01:20] Nina Patel: That's a common pattern. two main approaches: 1) keep your ES shortlist, then call Redwood hosted endpoint for embeddings + rerank; 2) run vector search in a vector DB (Milvus/Pinecone) and either call Redwood to rerank or run the whole stack on Redwood Dedicated with colocated vector store depending on latency/throughput needs.
[01:35] Samir Das: Latency is key - our SLOs are 200ms p95 for search requests. can Redwood meet that if we do ES shortlist (500 doc) -> embedding rerank?
[01:45] Nina Patel: For hosted, end-to-end you'll typically see p95 around 120-250ms depending on model size, batch settings, and network hop. dedicated in-region will be lower and more predictable. if you use batching and small model quantization, you can push p95 under 150ms for 500-doc rerank.
[01:58] Marcus Lee: What about throughput - during peak we expect sustained 120 QPS and spikes to 200 QPS for short windows. how does batching play with that?
[02:07] Arjun Mehta: Batching helps amortize model latency but increases tail latency for single-user requests. Redwood's runtime supports dynamic batching and configurable latency SLOs; for 120-200 QPS and 500-doc rerank, you'd likely need dedicated capacity or scale-hosted with autoscale + burst capacity.
[02:22] Priya Rao: For the embeddings dimensionality - we're testing 768 vs 1024. curious about storage and latency implications and how quantization affects retrieval quality.
[02:31] Nina Patel: 768 is common; 1024 gives slight quality bump for some models but increases storage and compute. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles - 8-bit or 4-bit post-training quantization for vectors reduces storage and can be fine for reranking if you validate. we also support on-the-fly quantized inference kernels in the runtime to keep latency low.
[02:47] Priya Rao: When you say quantized inference kernels, do you mean the reranker model runs on quantized weights too?
[02:52] Arjun Mehta: yes, some model architectures are robust to 8-bit quantization for rerank heads. the runtime selects kernels that are quantization-friendly. that reduces GPU memory and improves throughput.
[03:03] Elena Gomez: From a security perspective we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration. can Redwood provide audit logs per request and optional customer-managed keys?
[03:12] Jamie Clarke: yes, hosted offers SOC2 compliance and audit logs; Dedicated adds VPC peering and can be configured with customer-managed KMS for encryption. Private deployment gives you full control in your VPC and can be air-gapped for extra compliance. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:25] Marcus Lee: Good. on the vector DB side, if we keep Milvus, how do we avoid double-network hops? every search would be ES -> Milvus -> Redwood -> ES? that's too many hops.
[03:36] Nina Patel: Right, ideal flow is ES shortlist locally, fetch embedding vectors from your vector store colocated with ES (same cluster/region) and then call Redwood rerank endpoint with candidate doc embeddings or IDs plus features. another option: push reranking logic into Redwood Dedicated where we host vector store and reranker together to reduce network hops - that's the Dedicated/private pattern.
[03:54] Samir Das: If we host vector store with Redwood Dedicated, who manages the vector DB? is that part of the offering or do we bring our own?
[04:02] Arjun Mehta: For Dedicated, we can run the managed vector store as part of the cluster or integrate with your managed Milvus. there's flexibility - some customers prefer Redwood managed to simplify ops; others bring their own and we integrate via fast internal networking.
[04:15] Priya Rao: On cost, what's the rough monthly for Dedicated to handle 200 QPS peaks for rerank? ballpark is fine.
[04:22] Jamie Clarke: ballpark depends on model size and region. rough estimate for a dedicated pool to handle sustained 120 QPS with 200 QPS spikes for 500-doc rerank might be X to Y (redacted in transcript) - we'll follow up with exact pricing tiers. pricing depends on reserved GPU hours, support level, and data retention.
[04:39] Marcus Lee: For benchmarks, what should we provide?
[04:42] Nina Patel: Ideally: sample query log (anonymized), representative candidate set sizes (e.g., 500), dataset vector sizes and dimensionality, and expected SLA. we'll run an initial hosted bench and then a dedicated run to show differences.
[04:54] Priya Rao: We can provide a 10k query sample and sample docs this week.
[04:58] Elena Gomez: We need to understand failure modes - what happens if Dedicated node fails during a promo? how does autoscaling and fallback to hosted work?
[05:08] Arjun Mehta: Redwood has smart routing and automatic fallback policies. Dedicated can be configured with regional fallbacks to hosted; requests will route to an alternate model variant if capacity constrained. we also support canary rollouts and gradual traffic shifts.
[05:20] Samir Das: For observability, we need per-route latency and token cost breakdowns - to show product managers.
[05:26] Nina Patel: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks. for rerank use case, we can surface per-request latency and per-model cost.
[05:35] Marcus Lee: On hybrid search - we plan to keep BM25 shortlist and dense rerank. any guidance on candidate set size where embeddings make sense?
[05:43] Nina Patel: In general, embeddings help most when candidate set small enough to rerank within latency SLOs. 100-1000 candidates is common; if your BM25 recall is high, smaller candidate set (100-300) reduces cost and improves latencies. also consider learned rerankers that use sparse + dense features.
[05:58] Priya Rao: Are there examples of customers that moved from ES+Milvus PoC to Redwood Dedicated and what improvements they saw?
[06:05] Jamie Clarke: We can anonymize a case study - common improvements: 20-40% p95 latency reduction after colocation and kernel optimization, and 10-30% cost savings via batching/quantization and optimized kernels. we'll send a short case study doc.
[06:18] Marcus Lee: About dimensionality - if we shift from 1024->768 with quantization, any rule of thumb for quality degradation?
[06:25] Arjun Mehta: It depends on model and dataset. sometimes 768 with 8-bit quant performs nearly identically; other times 1024 gives better separation. Redwood Optimize runs small A/B evals on your eval set to quantify drop.
[06:36] Elena Gomez: We have strict data residency - EU for EU users. can Dedicated be placed in our preferred region?
[06:42] Nina Patel: Yes, Dedicated can be provisioned in-region, and Private deployments allow full regional control. hosted is multi-region but we can pin region for data residency.
[06:50] Priya Rao: On model lifecycle: we want to pin model versions and have rollback. how does Redwood handle model rollouts?
[06:57] Arjun Mehta: Redwood supports model pinning, canary deploys, A/B testing and automatic fallback to older variants. rollouts are configured per-route.
[07:05] Marcus Lee: Any constraints on embedding dimensions for vector DBs you support? e.g., some managed services limit dimensionality or charge by vector size.
[07:13] Nina Patel: We don't impose hard limits on dimensions; but managed vector stores might. cost scales linearly with dimension and storage; that's part of our Optimize recommendations.
[07:22] Priya Rao: For our PoC, we want to try: 1) hosted quick test with 100 queries, 2) dedicated run with sample data, 3) evaluation of 768 vs 1024 and 8-bit vs 4-bit quant. timeline target: decision within 4 weeks.
[07:35] Jamie Clarke: Sounds reasonable. we'll send the security pack and bench template. can we plan the dedicated throughput run for next week?
[07:41] Marcus Lee: yes, next week works.

[07:48] -- Mid-call technical deep dive (Nina + Priya) --
[08:00] [08:00] Nina Patel: quick deep dive - what reranker model are you thinking? is it a cross-encoder that takes both query and doc text or a bi-encoder + cross for rerank?
[08:09] Priya Rao: We prototyped a cross-encoder for top-50 but it's too slow. we want a bi-encoder for initial dense score then a lightweight cross-encoder rerank for top-200.
[08:18] Arjun Mehta: That's a good pattern. bi-encoder for vector similarity (fast), then cross-encoder for heavy ranking on smaller set. Redwood's runtime supports both and can chain calls; for example, bi-encoder hosted indexing + ANN search then cross-encoder rerank collocated.
[08:31] Marcus Lee: For ANN index - are you recommending HNSW or IVF/OPQ? we tried HNSW but memory was big.
[08:37] Nina Patel: HNSW gives great recall and low-latency but memory intensive; IVF+OPQ (with product quant) is more memory efficient and works better for larger corpora. for rerank use case where you have a short list, HNSW is often fine if you have enough RAM.
[08:50] Priya Rao: How does Redwood handle stateful caches (KV cache) for autoregressive models - maybe less relevant here but curious for other features.
[08:57] Arjun Mehta: Redwood runtime manages KV cache for decoder-only models to speed up generation. for rerank cross-encoders it doesn't apply. but caching candidate embeddings is common; we have prefix/KV-like caches for embedding computation to avoid repeated encodes on same docs.
[09:10] Nina Patel: also consider hybrid features - sparse BM25 score + dense vector score as features into a learned reranker. that often outperforms pure dense rerank.
[09:19] Marcus Lee: good note.

[09:25] -- Questions from Argus legal/security (Elena) --
[09:30] Elena Gomez: A few compliance Qs: Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) in hosted? can logs be forwarded to our SIEM?
[09:37] Jamie Clarke: Hosted supports KMS integration and we can forward audit logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 ingestion. for full CMK control, Dedicated or Private is preferred.
[09:46] Elena Gomez: What about data retention and deletion policies?
[09:49] Nina Patel: We support configurable retention windows and can enable no-persist mode for sensitive workloads. we'll include details in the security pack.

[09:56] -- Pricing and procurement --
[10:03] Marcus Lee: procurement will want committed spend options. expected procurement timeline?
[10:06] Jamie Clarke: Typical timeline: PoC -> procurement due diligence (security + legal) -> committed Dedicated contract or hosted subscription. could be 4-8 weeks depending on procurement.

[10:15] -- Closing recap --
[10:18] Jamie Clarke: Recap: Argus will share sample queries/dataset; Redwood will share security docs, bench template, and case study. plan hosted quick test then dedicated throughput run. action owners and due dates listed in action items.
[10:28] Marcus Lee: thanks everyone, we'll get the sample dataset to Priya and Jamie by Thursday.
[10:33] Jamie Clarke: Great - thanks all. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench next week.
[10:40] (call ended)
